newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ford, Chrysler said keen on Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Ford, Chrysler said keen on Philippines.

text.p: Ford Motor Co and Chrysler Corp were interested in investing in the Philippines though they had not yet indicated what sort of facilities they wanted to set up, a Philippine official said on Tuesday.

"We've been talking to a lot of interested players in the automotive industry. GM is only one of them ... Ford is also looking. Chrysler is also looking," Board of Investments (BOI) managing head Melito Salazar told reporters.

Last year, the Philippines lost out to Thailand in a fierce competition for a multi-million dollar General Motors (GM) investment. GM decided to locate in Thailand a production unit catering to its Asia Pacific market.
But GM would like to set up a components factory in the Philippines, Salazar said.
Salazar said Ford had sent a team to take a "serious look" at the country, while Chrysler Corp had plans to tie up with a local company.
The Philippines is reviewing its investment plan for the automotive industry, which is at present dominated by Japanese firms.
The plan, which may include new tariff and tax rates for car components, is expected to be completed later this month or early next month.
